title: Pre-Analysis Review — Impact Resistant Cargo Lining Against the Aft Compartment Work
abstract: Closed review of the in-production impact resistant lining panel, raised to sequence it against the aft compartment structural and detection work that has to reach the same wall behind it.

sections.objective: Sequence the impact resistant lining panel against the other work planned behind the same compartment wall, and decide whether its retrofit bulletin can open while a structural reinforcement and a detection change are still in pre-analysis on the same compartment. The review was raised internally by the cabin office, which had no wish to install a panel standard twice on the same aircraft.
sections.findings_summary: Four items were confirmed and the answer was a sequencing one rather than a design one. The dual wavelength detector candidate mounts on the compartment ceiling and its detector footprint sits inside the light strip housing moulded into the new panel. Installing the panel first and the detector afterwards means cutting a moulded panel on the aircraft, which is not a repair anyone should be doing. The sill frame reinforcement in pre-analysis needs the same panels out. The bulletin as issued has no concurrency statement, and the illustrated part list carries the light strip as a separate item that the moulding absorbs.
sections.next_steps: Hold the retrofit bulletin until the detector candidate has fixed its footprint, and add a concurrency statement rather than letting operators plan the two independently. Give the sill frame work order the panel removal sequence so it is written once. Re-issue the illustrated part list with the light strip absorbed into the panel item and the old strip marked pre-mod.

similarity_seeds: panel damage rate driven by short sector baggage handling
equipment mounted on the cargo compartment ceiling wall

tasks.title: Compare the detector footprint with the light strip housing
Search candidate work behind the same compartment wall
Review the bulletin for a concurrency statement

expected_findings.rationale: The dual wavelength detector mounts inside the compartment on the same ceiling line as the moulded light strip housing. If the panel is installed first the detector cannot be fitted without cutting a moulded panel on the aircraft, which no repair scheme covers.
expected_findings.resolution: Retrofit bulletin held until the detector footprint is fixed; a concurrency statement added so operators do not plan the two independently.

expected_findings.rationale: The bulletin is effective on the whole in-service population with no concurrency statement and no reference to the compartment work in pre-analysis. It cannot open in that form without creating a population that has to be revisited.
expected_findings.resolution: Effectivity re-issued with a concurrency statement and a hold until the detector candidate is launched or dropped.

expected_findings.rationale: The sill frame reinforcement works the structure directly behind these panels and needs them out. Two work orders were about to write the same panel removal sequence with different torque and sealing call-outs.
expected_findings.resolution: Panel removal sequence issued to the sill frame work order to be referenced rather than rewritten.

expected_findings.rationale: The figure lists the compartment light strip as an item in its own right. On the new panel the strip is inside the moulding and has no separate part number, so an order against the old item number returns something that cannot be fitted.
expected_findings.resolution: Figure re-issued with the strip absorbed into the panel item and the old item marked pre-mod.

expected_non_findings.reason: Ranked high by similarity because both replace segmented light fittings with a continuous strip, and both are described in almost the same words, but it is a passenger cabin change with no cargo compartment content and no shared part or zone.

type_data.conclusion: Validated. No design change is needed, but the bulletin cannot open until the detector footprint is fixed and a concurrency statement is in place.
